learning_outcomes.text: Students can classify the tasks and role of modern human resource management in organizations.
Students can evaluate essential instruments of personnel recruitment, acquisition, and development regarding their suitability and applicability.
Students can practically apply relevant theoretical concepts and models of communication and sustainably solve problems that may arise in communication processes.
Students can recognize the importance of learning in the context of change and transformation and create conditions for successful individual and collective learning processes.
Students can explain, review, and reflect on the utility of the principles of organizational theoretical foundations using practical examples.
Students can evaluate forms of primary and secondary organization regarding their applicability and context-specific relevance.
Students can utilize relevant concepts of sustainable organizational change in professional practice for co-design and assess their significance for entrepreneurial activity.

Students can name important key competencies (e.g., social competencies, sustainability competencies) and reflect on and evaluate the requirements of the current and future working world against the background of their own competencies.
Students can classify essential concepts and theories of personnel leadership and reflect on the success of leadership.
Students can recognize and evaluate the particular relevance of sustainability as an essential element of human resource management, personnel leadership, and organization.

syllabus_topics: Meaning, goals, tasks, and selected instruments of personnel management
Fundamentals of organization theories, structural and process organization
Organizational forms, primary and secondary organization
teaching_methods: Seminar-style instruction with exercises and case studies
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
